idiom_name: case class with named/default parameters; copy for variants
implementation_notes: A case class constructor already requires every non-default parameter (the compiler rejects missing arguments) and named parameters make argument order irrelevant, so Scala's local idiom replaces the staged builder for ordinary data objects; copy() covers 'the same value with one field changed'. When a sequence must be enforced at the type level, the staged form is written by hand - one class (or one type-parameterized builder) per step - or via singleton types in Scala 3; that is rare, because the constructor plus named arguments already give the unskippable-required-data guarantee that the pattern exists to provide. Prefer the case class and keep the staged builder for side-effecting setup or APIs consumed from dynamically typed callers.
pitfalls: Named arguments prevent swaps, not invalid values: type-level presence is not a domain rule, so validate with require() or a smart constructor.
Default parameter expressions are evaluated per call; a mutable default (a ListBuffer, an ArrayBuffer) shared across instances is a classic aliasing bug - use immutable defaults.
Case class equality and pattern matching make adding or reordering a field a source-compatible but semantically breaking change for downstream matchers and copy() call sites.
